text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Pakistan bought 500,000 tonnes of wheat Thursday, including 350,000 tonnes from the United States, 100,000 from Australia and 50,000 from Canada, U.S. exporters and the Pakistan embassy said. Shipment was for July 11 to August 10. The embassy said sellers were Louis Dreyfus, Cargill, the Canadian Wheat Board, Marubeni in Australia and the U.S., Kanematsu and United Grain Growers. The lowest price was US$140.00 per tonne FOB. Most of the U.S. share will be for August shipment when new crop is available.

WHEAT SALES - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd bought 21,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Marubeni Corp, company officials said. Cheiljedang bought 3,200 tonnes of soft white (10 percent protein) at $0.43 of CBOT Sept SRW futures, 500 of soft white (9.5 percent) at $0.41 over CBOT Sept SRW, 4,000 hard red winter (HRW) at $0.52 over KCBT Sept HRW and 3,300 dark northern spring (DNS) at $1.06 over MGE Sept. Dongah bought 4,500 soft white (10 percent protein) at $140.73 per tonne FOB, 1,500 soft white (9.5 percent) at $139.99, 3,500 HRW at $147.25, and 1,000 DNS at $172.51.

WHEAT SALES - Algeria bought up to 275,000 tonnes of wheat, around half of it from the United States, European grain traders said. Pricing details were sketchy but exporters said U.S. hard red winter wheat was priced between $162 and $163 per tonne, cost and freight. Algeria also purchased wheat of optional origin at around $160 per tonne, including cost and freight. Algeria had initially sought 150,000 tonnes of wheat for second half August and September shipment.

BARLEY SALE - Saudi Arabia on Thursday confirmed buying one million tonnes of barley at $142 to $148 per tonne, European grain traders said. The barley is for arrival in September and October and the origin is left to the seller's option. It is likely to be supplied partly from the European Union, but a decision would depend on Brussels agreeing to unblock export subsidies which are currently frozen ahead of the harvest. Other possible suppliers include Australia, Canada and the United States, although Canada's state-sponsored marketing board has indicated it has little barley to offer at present.

CORN SALE - The Korea Feedgrain Purchase Committee bought 50,000 tonnes of corn from Toepfer at $125.47 a tonne C&F, traders said. Arrival was set for October 10 to the western port of Inchon. Shipment was set for August 22-September 10 from the U.S. Gulf and for September 11-30 from the Pacific Northwest. The seller can also deliver Chinese corn at $121.47 a tonne C&F, they said.

SOYMEAL SALE - South Korea's Korea Feed Association bought 30,000 to 35,000 tonnes of soymeal at $276.50 per tonne, C&F, traders said. Toepfer sold the soymeal with the arrival by Oct 20 to the western port of Inchon.
